Synopsis:
The player inspects the egg, having never seen anything like it before. In addition to taking or destroying it, they can do a variety of other odd things with the egg - including commune with the unborn gith inside.

Cluster Contexts:
- CRE_Hatchery_Egg.json: The player has come upon a strange githyanki egg — its shell is alien and you can make out a vague form inside — and can choose to take it, destroy it, or attempt more unusual actions such as communing with the unborn gith. Off‑screen the scene sits in or near a gith creche/infirmary, so creche guardians and other githyanki (and their leaders’ interests) are likely nearby and hostile if they learn of interference. Earlier beats tied to the Zaith'isk device, Vlaakith’s orders, a missing gith “weapon,” and requests from an expeditioner all raise the stakes: this isn’t just a salvage job but a moral and political choice with consequences for gith loyalties. How companions like Laezel or figures such as Daisy react will depend on those prior events — Laezel’s loyalty to Vlaakith and recent shocks around the Zaith'isk, and Daisy’s claim to be hunted for hiding secrets, will color responses.
- CRE_Hatchery_Caretaker.json: You've entered a gith creche hatchery where Varsh Ko'kuu is the long-serving caretaker of a single stubborn, unhatched egg he clearly cherishes—he even survived a rough hatching himself and treats late arrivals with special sympathy. Off‑screen, Kith'rak Therezzyn (the creche captain) expects weak or slow eggs to be destroyed and could inspect the hatchery at any time, which is why Varsh is anxious and torn. Lae'zel, a githyanki warrior tied to Vlaakith, is present and contemptuous of the egg, so the player—an outsider called an istik—enters a fraught moment where they can learn lore about gith eggs or try to convince Varsh to entrust the last egg to them. Nearby tensions (the creche’s guards, recent Zaith'isk events, and prior requests to retrieve eggs) make any attempt to remove or protect the egg risky and morally loaded.
- CRE_Expeditioner.json: You and your party are approaching a githyanki crèche on a rocky roof (there’s also a skittish bird guarding a nest of baked goods nearby), when an aging expeditioner, Lady Esther, stops you. She claims the Society of Brilliance commissioned her to procure a githyanki egg so they can incubate and raise the hatchling in a peaceful tradition, but she was chased and insulted when she tried to buy one and is still indignant about it. The conversation centers on whether a githyanki’s violence is innate or taught—Lady Esther is contemptuous of the Society’s optimism, while the player may argue nurture and Lae’zel vehemently opposes stealing any gith child. Lady Esther asks the player to help infiltrate the crèche and acquire an egg, promising reward if you succeed.
- GLO_Laezel_WRD_GithEggRelated.json: Dialog with Laezel regarding the Gith egg.- Conversation about just taking it from the hatchery- Conversation after players give the egg to Lady Esther- If players kept it in Act3:- - Conversation about how the egg is doing. Reactivity based on whether it's in Laezel's inventory. Later in epilogue, if it was in her inventory, it would be hatched and she would be mentioning it.- If players lose the egg or get it destroyed before reaching Act3:- - Laezel is not yet attached to it, so she mentions that it wouldn't have survived anyway- If players lose the egg or get it destroyed after reaching Act3:- - Conversation about Laezel being mad at you for not taking good enough care of it- If players gave it to Lady Esther, after seeing the hatched gith in Act3:- - Conversation about what happened to the kid and how he turned out, depending on Laezel's current views and outcomes of the situation (boy attacked you and you killed him OR convinced him that you're good or he's flawed in his beliefs and he didn't attack you)Follow up in Epilogue:- If Laezel kept the egg, it hatches and she can talk more about it- If players kept the egg or left it in camp, it hatches and we get a Gazette update about it- If players destroyed or misplaced the egg, it's not mentioned in the epilogue
- LOW_TheLodge_GithBoy.json: Dialog file for Ptaris, the Gith born from the egg given to Esther. The player enters on a scene of devestation, Ptaris the only being still alive. Hatched unnaturally from his egg and experimented on in the name of making him 'good', he has developed uncanny psionic powers, and used them to murder everyone who failed to live up to his strict moral code.

context: You’ve come upon a strange githyanki egg — its shell is alien and you can make out a vague form inside — sitting in or near a gith creche where you can examine it, take it, destroy it, or attempt unusual acts like communing with the unborn. Off‑screen Varsh Ko’kuu is the long‑serving caretaker who clearly cherishes this particular egg, while creche captain Kith’rak Therezzyn expects weak eggs destroyed and could arrive to inspect at any time. Laezel, tied to Vlaakith, is present and contemptuous of any theft or sentimentality, and an aging expeditioner (Lady Esther) has already asked you to procure an egg for the Society of Brilliance. Recent beats involving the Zaith’isk device, Vlaakith’s orders, a missing gith “weapon,” and expeditioner requests mean this is more than salvage — your choice has moral and political consequences and may make gith guardians or your companions hostile.
